samples.summary: §7's derived label limit still reads only the complementarity payload, so it asserts "no validity label does" and "there is still no precision … figure anywhere above" in the same render where the new §6 prints one
samples.evidence: `labelsLimit(s)` (scripts/agent/eval/report.mjs:2774-2792) takes its whole input from `s.complementarity.label_store` and hard-states, at line 2784-2790, `"…adjudicated PAIR label(s) exist …, and no validity label does"` plus `"**So there is still no precision, recall or correctness figure anywhere above**"`. This PR adds a second, independent source of truth for exactly that premise — `s.validity` — and `labelsLimit` was not updated to consult it. The PR's own new fixture proves the contradicting render exists: `report.test.mjs`'s `labelledValidity()` makes §6 render `0.667 (n=6 labelled findings)` for `precision` (asserted at report.test.mjs ~2140: `/metric=precision\/arm=panel\/tier=gold\/stratum=all` \| 0\.667 \(n=6 labelled findings\)/`), while §7 in the very same document still says no validity label exists and no precision figure appears above. The comment at report.mjs:2769-2772 states the intent this misses — "a store with validity labels in it would change what §7 says rather than leaving §7 confidently wrong" — but the only census it reads is the pair-label one. Fix belongs in `labelsLimit`, which should take the validity section's `labels`/`metrics` as well.

samples.summary: The driver's tolerated exit code (1) is the same code validity.mjs uses for its hard failures, so the "exited N. Nothing was filed" refusal no longer fires for a genuine validity crash
samples.evidence: `score-all.mjs:721-722` now accepts `status === step.partial_exit` (1) for the validity step before anything is parsed. But `validity.mjs` uses exit 1 for real failures too, not only for a `partial` verdict: `process.exit(1)` at validity.mjs:1172 ("corpus version … does not exist under this root"), validity.mjs:1199 ("run … does not exist under this root") and validity.mjs:1266 (the top-level `main().catch` — every `refuse()` inside `scoreValidity`, e.g. a label filed under another corpus version, `assertOnePopulation`, `assertComparableWindow`). For all of those the driver skips its dedicated exit-code refusal and falls through to the JSON-parse branch (score-all.mjs:726-728), so a genuine crash is reported as `"validity.mjs exited 1 and its --json output does not parse … 0 byte(s) on stdout"` — a message that blames a malformed payload for a store/argument error, and one that `assertPartialIsDeclared`'s three carefully-worded refusals never get to state. The scorer would need a distinct exit code (or a machine-readable partial marker) for the tolerance to be as narrow as its doc comment claims.

samples.summary: `lensSignature` compares RAW snapshot lens fields, so replicates that report.mjs has already proven are one reviewer (identical `config_hash`) can be rendered as "not replicates of one reviewer" with the lens table blanked
samples.evidence: `reviewerFigures`' `lensSignature` (report.mjs:1488-1491) joins `stated(l[c.key])` for `model/samples/effort/gating` straight off the stored snapshot, and any difference becomes a `disagreements` row plus an empty `lenses` table (report.mjs:1540-1547) and the 🔴 "axis(es) of the reviewer's identity DISAGREE" block (report.mjs:1698). `config-hash.mjs` is the module of record for what makes two lenses the same reviewer and it compares EFFECTIVE values: `config-hash.mjs:234` — `effort: lens.effort === undefined ? DEFAULT_EFFORT : String(lens.effort)` — with the comment at config-hash.mjs:137 spelling out that "a lens that sets no `effort` hashes identically to a lens that writes `\"high\"` out"; `samples`/`maxTurns` are likewise coerced. Meanwhile report.mjs's own CLI already refuses any run whose `config_hash` differs (report.mjs:2971-2974), so every replicate reaching `reviewerFigures` is hash-identical by construction. A snapshot pair that differs only in an omitted-vs-explicit `effort` (or `samples: 1` vs `"1"`) therefore prints a red "these are not replicates of one reviewer and no figure in this report may be read as a property of either" over a reviewer the store can prove is one. The comparison should go through `config-hash.mjs`'s canonical lens form rather than raw fields.

samples.summary: The scheduled lane's own documentation still describes the pre-validity cost and step count (175 calls, five scorers, seven filings, eight files) after this PR moved them to 210, six, eight and nine
samples.evidence: `.github/workflows/eval-score.yml:83` — "each tick costs about 175 GitHub API calls against a 5000/hour budget shared with the review panel"; the new `API_READERS`/`estimateApiCalls` model in this diff makes the same 7-item K=3 tick cost 210 (`score-all.test.mjs:189` asserts exactly that). Line 265 — "both checkouts, the API budget preflight, five scorers, seven filings, the render" — is now six scorers and eight filings (`STEPS` gained `validity`, and `writtenPaths` gains one cross-run path). Line 253 — "two full passes over unchanged inputs produce byte-identical output across all eight files" — is now nine files (3 volume + 5 cross-run + 1 report), which is also what the staging step's `written-paths.txt` will contain. Nothing enforces these numbers, so they are the only description of the lane's cost a reader of the workflow gets.

samples.summary: score-all.mjs's module header still counts the sequence as "SIX STEPS in a YAML file" while the rest of the header was renumbered to six scorers / seven steps
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/eval/score-all.mjs:5` — "WHY THIS IS A MODULE AND NOT SIX STEPS IN A YAML FILE" — was left at six while the surrounding prose in the same diff moved to "six merged scorers" and `STEPS` is documented as "The seven steps" (score-all.mjs:75). The sequence is now seven children (six scorers + the renderer).

verdict.reason: Verified as described. `labelsLimit` (report.mjs:2774-2792) derives its entire premise from `s.complementarity.label_store` (2775) and both branches hard-state that no validity label exists (2784) and that "there is still no precision, recall or correctness figure anywhere above" (2787-2788); the zero-store branch (2778-2779) makes the same absolute claim. The change adds an independent second source for that premise: `validityFigures` (1197) produces `precision` cells and `renderReport` emits `renderValidity(s.validity)` at 1657 immediately before `renderLimits(r)` at 1658, so both sections always appear in one document. §6 is new — `.trusted/scripts/agent/eval/report.mjs` has no `renderValidity`/`validityFigures`, while its `labelsLimit` (.trusted:2152-2166) carries identical prose, confirming the dependent consumer was left unchanged. The repo's own fixture proves the contradicting render: `labelledValidity()` (report.test.mjs:1895-1913) is rendered through the full report at report.test.mjs:2050 and asserted to print `0.667 (n=6 labelled findings)` for precision at report.test.mjs:2056, in the same document where §7 denies any validity label or precision figure. The comment at report.mjs:2769-2772 states the intent the code misses. No guard prevents this: nothing in `renderLimits` or `labelsLimit` inspects `s.validity`. In-lane (unupdated consumer of a changed contract, broken site outside the new code) and blocking at major.

verdict.reason: The tolerance at score-all.mjs:721-722 is real (partial_exit: 1 at score-all.mjs:106), and validity.mjs really does exit 1 on hard failures (validity.mjs:1172, 1199, and main().catch at 1264-1266 over the throwing refuse() at 83-85). But those paths cannot reach the protected operation. --json is always passed (score-all.mjs:578) and the payload is written to stdout only at validity.mjs:1255, after scoreValidity succeeds and before the exit code is set at 1260 — so every crash path exits with empty stdout and is caught by the very next guard, JSON.parse at score-all.mjs:725-729, which refuses before anything is parsed into a score; and even with a payload, assertPartialIsDeclared (score-all.mjs:454-467) refuses on a missing or non-"partial" completeness.verdict. Nothing is filed and the lane still aborts, and the child's real error is echoed to the operator's stderr at score-all.mjs:602 immediately before the refusal. What is left is a less precise refusal message and an overstated doc comment (score-all.mjs:436-443) — minor under this rubric, not a reachable guard bypass or a broken caller.

verdict.reason: Code is present as described. report.mjs:1488-1491 builds `lensSignature` from raw snapshot fields via `stated()` (report.mjs:1405) over LENS_COLUMNS (report.mjs:1417-1422), with no canonicalisation and no use of config-hash.mjs. config-hash.mjs is the module of record and normalises effective values: effort at :234 with the explicit equivalence comment at :136-140, gating at :223, samples via sampleCountFor at :215. config-build.mjs:206-208 and the materializeLenses docblock at :236-241 confirm snapshots keep raw manifest lens fields, deliberately preserving an absent `effort` key, so two hash-identical snapshots can differ in these fields. Both guards compare by config_hash only (report.mjs:2971-2974 for the CLI; store.mjs:828-838 for putRun), so such a pair reaches reviewerFigures, produces a disagreements row (report.mjs:1503-1508), blanks the lens table (report.mjs:1527-1533), and prints the red "not replicates of one reviewer / no figure ... may be read as a property of either" block (report.mjs:1700-1704). This is a violated cross-module invariant (config_hash defines same-reviewer) with a consumer contradicting it — in the blast-radius lane, major impact. Only defect in the finding is minor line-number drift for the blanked-table cite (1540-1547 vs actual 1527-1533), which does not affect the substance.
